rules.title: Security deposit cap of one month's rent (general rule)
rules.requirement: A landlord may not demand or receive security in an amount or value above one month's rent, in addition to the first month's rent paid on or before initial occupancy. Draft coverage excludes owners who appear to meet the small-landlord test in (c)(5), which carries a separate two-month cap that is not drafted here.
rules.quoted_span: a landlord shall not demand or receive security, however denominated, in an amount or value in excess of an amount equal to one month’s rent, in addition to any rent for the first month paid on or before initial occupancy
rules.exemptions: Per (c)(2), an advance payment of not less than six months' rent is not prohibited if the lease term is six months or longer. Per (c)(3), a landlord and tenant may agree to alterations at the tenant's request for a specified fee. Per (c)(5), qualifying small landlords are subject to a two-month cap instead. Per (c)(6), the subdivision does not apply to security collected or demanded before July 1, 2024. Lease term and alteration agreements cannot be represented in the coverage fields.
rules.interaction: Paragraph (c)(5) sets a separate two-month cap for qualifying natural-person or LLC landlords. That cap is not drafted because its service-member carve-out cannot be encoded.

rules.title: No deduction from security for preexisting damage or ordinary wear and tear
rules.requirement: A landlord may not assert a claim against the tenant or the security for damages or defective conditions that preexisted the tenancy, or for ordinary wear and tear or its effects.
rules.quoted_span: The landlord shall not assert a claim against the tenant or the security for damages to the premises or any defective conditions that preexisted the tenancy, for ordinary wear and tear or the effects thereof

rules.title: Written notice of the tenant's option to request an initial inspection
rules.requirement: Within a reasonable time after notice of intent to terminate the tenancy, or before the end of the lease term, the landlord must notify the tenant in writing of the option to request an initial inspection and of the right to be present at it.
rules.quoted_span: the landlord shall notify the tenant in writing of the tenant’s option to request an initial inspection and of the tenant’s right to be present at the inspection
rules.exemptions: Per (f)(7), the subdivision does not apply when the tenancy is terminated under Code of Civil Procedure § 1161 subdivision (2), (3), or (4). Per (f)(1), if the tenant chooses not to request an initial inspection, the landlord's duties under the subdivision are discharged. The termination basis cannot be represented in the coverage fields.

rules.title: Photographs of the unit at the start of the tenancy
rules.requirement: For tenancies that begin on or after July 1, 2025, the landlord must photograph the unit immediately before, or at the inception of, the tenancy.
rules.quoted_span: For tenancies that begin on or after July 1, 2025, the landlord shall take photographs of the unit immediately before, or at the
rules.interaction: The tenancy start date is not an available coverage field, so the July 1, 2025 applicability is stated in the requirement and effective_date.

rules.title: Photographs after possession returned and after repairs or cleanings
rules.requirement: Beginning April 1, 2025, the landlord must photograph the unit within a reasonable time after possession is returned and before any repairs or cleanings for which a deduction or claim will be made. The landlord must also photograph the unit within a reasonable time after those repairs or cleanings are completed.
rules.quoted_span: Beginning April 1, 2025, the landlord shall take photographs of the unit within a reasonable time after the possession of the unit is returned to the landlord

rules.title: Itemized statement and return of security within 21 calendar days
rules.requirement: No later than 21 calendar days after the tenant has vacated, the landlord must furnish an itemized statement of the basis for and amount of security received and its disposition, and return any remaining portion. Delivery methods and rules for multiple adult tenants are set out in (h)(1)(A)-(C).
rules.quoted_span: No later than 21 calendar days after the tenant has vacated the premises
rules.exemptions: The text states the 21-day period runs from vacating, but not earlier than a termination notice under CCP § 1161 or Civil Code § 1946/1946.1, or 60 days before a fixed-term lease expires. Subparagraph (h)(3), which is cut off at the end of this chunk, may address repairs that cannot be completed within 21 days.
